subject: barn owls
one_liner: Payment infrastructure for barn owls, the last workforce still settling in voles.
brand_voice_notes: Deadpan merchant-services copy written for a bird. The company never acknowledges that owls cannot read, sign contracts, or hold a card. Every sentence treats rodent control as a regulated trade with invoices, settlement windows, and an audit trail. Numbers are stated with total confidence and are always slightly wrong in a way nobody at the company has noticed. No winking. No exclamation marks. The funniest line in any block is delivered as a compliance footnote.

hero.sub: Pellet is the merchant stack for nocturnal rodent-remediation contractors. Take payment at the loft door, settle before sunrise, and keep a bone-level audit trail your accountant will decline to open.

features.title: Pellet Reconciliation
features.blurb: Your owl brings up the night's work around 5am. The reader photographs the pellet, sorts the skeletons by species, and matches each femur against an open invoice line. Anything that does not pair is flagged before the barn wakes up.

features.title: Silent Tap
features.blurb: A payment chime at 2am ends the hunt for everyone in the field. Our terminal confirms with haptics only. Owls cannot feel haptics, so we also send an email.

features.title: Loft Terminal
features.blurb: Weatherproof to minus twenty, mounted on the entry beam, charged by the bird's own perching weight. Holding a full charge takes roughly forty landings a night. Most barn owls land six times.

demo_screen_concept: TONIGHT'S LEDGER, a merchant settlement console for a single barn-owl operator on the night of 17 September. A left rail of shift counters (catches, gross grams, unsettled lines, pellets in queue, next deposit clock). A center table with one row per rodent: capture time, species, mass in grams, property serviced, fee, and settlement state. Species filter chips (field vole, wood mouse, common shrew, brown rat, unidentified) plus a settled/unsettled toggle and a fake search box. Clicking a row opens a receipt modal with the fee breakdown and a skeletal match readout. A primary 'Run pellet reconciliation' button steps through queued pellets against unsettled rows one at a time with a ticking status line, settles most of them, and flags exactly one mismatch that the operator can dismiss or escalate.

images.rationale: Full budget spent, 1 hero + 3 testimonial headshots. Hero earned it because the design direction is a photo-led hardware corridor that opens on a full-bleed equipment shot, and the subject is a bird in a barn at night, which is exactly what the palette wants. Demo assets skipped because the demo_screen_concept is a settlement ledger table, not a photo-shaped surface, so every pixel there is type and rules. Headshots earned it because the testimonials are attributed to named barn owls with corporate titles, and a deadpan employee-portrait owl is the whole joke in one frame.

items.prompt: Editorial night photograph of a single barn owl perched on a weathered wooden beam inside a dark barn loft, pale heart-shaped face turned toward the camera, wings folded, shot slightly from below on a long lens with shallow depth of field. Cold moonlight rakes in from a loft opening above and behind the bird, rimming the feather edges in pale zinc-blue #6FA8C7 against a near-black #0D1215 interior. A single small equipment-yellow #F2B417 glint off galvanized metal hardware sits far out of focus in the background. Dusty air with visible motes in the moonbeam, desaturated cold industrial-agricultural mood, high contrast, deep shadows. One focal subject only. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.

design_direction.style: Agricultural equipment livery, moonlit galvanized dark mode. The page is staged as the flank of a machine parked in a barn after midnight: cold-rolled zinc panels, stencil-cut lettering, and one rationed hazard yellow that appears only where a hand is meant to go. There is no glass, no backdrop blur, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no newsprint or riso misregistration, no ground-glass amber, no leaded came, no moulded plastic, no plaster, no engraved guilloche, and no pharmaceutical fold. Light comes from one direction only, from above and slightly behind, the way a moon comes through a loft opening: every raised surface carries a 1px cold highlight on its top edge and nothing else. Shadows are hard, offset 3px down and 3px right, blur 0, pure black at 45 percent, because machine parts in a barn do not have soft shadows. Four motifs carry the whole page. (1) The zinc panel: sections and cards are #141C21 plates on the #0D1215 ground, 2px corner radius, hairline #2A363D border, with the cold top highlight and the hard offset shadow. (2) The rivet: a 6px circle, #2A363D fill with a 1px #47565E ring, set 10px in from each corner of every panel, four per plate, never decorative beyond that. (3) The hazard chevron: a 10px band of 45-degree stripes in equipment yellow #F2B417 on #0D1215, used exactly once per major section as the divider above its heading, and as the full-width bar under the primary CTA. (4) The spec plate: a tabular caps micro-row under every major heading, 10px, 0.16em tracking, #78888F, fields separated by hairline verticals, reading like a serial plate (MODEL / DUTY / RATED / SERIAL). Headings are condensed industrial caps in Big Shoulders Display, tracked +0.02em, set large and flush left. Body is Source Sans 3 at 17px, line-height 1.65, never centered below heading level. All figures, prices, masses, times, and ledger values are JetBrains Mono with tabular figures, because this is a company that counts mice. Yellow is rationed: primary CTA fill, chevron bands, the active nav dot, and nothing else. Moonlight zinc-blue #6FA8C7 carries links, active states, and data emphasis. The page composition is a vertical corridor: a full-bleed hero photograph of the bird, then a thin 1px spine running down the left gutter at 1024px and above that visually threads hero to features to pricing, so the scroll reads as one continuous machine rather than a stack of cards.

design_direction.archetype: Hardware-corridor landing page: full-bleed equipment hero with a pinned request-a-terminal bar, a spine-threaded scroll through three capability plates, a settlement-console teaser, operator testimonials as personnel cards, a three-plate rate table, and a closing stencil CTA.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Machinery, not UI. Nothing floats and nothing fades in from nowhere. Hover on a plate lifts it 2px and shortens its hard shadow to 2px, 120ms ease-out, like weight shifting on a mount. Buttons press down 1px and lose their shadow entirely on :active. The hazard chevron band under the primary CTA translates its stripes 10px on hover, 400ms linear, so it reads as a belt turning. Ledger rows in the demo highlight by swapping their left 2px border to zinc-blue with no transition at all, instantly, the way a mechanical indicator flips. The reconciliation run advances one row per 260ms with a mono status line updating in place. Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion by dropping to instant state changes.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed 16:9 photograph of a barn owl on a beam at night, bled to the top of the viewport with a bottom-anchored vertical scrim from transparent to #0D1215 so the headline sits on solid ground rather than on the bird. Stencil wordmark pinned top-left over the image with four corner rivets. The h1 is set in condensed caps at clamp(2.6rem, 7vw, 6rem) flush left against the left gutter spine, the sub capped at 62ch below it, then a horizontal request-a-terminal bar (email field plus yellow submit) directly under the CTA row and above the fold. A spec plate micro-row sits immediately beneath the wordmark reading MODEL PLT-2 / DUTY NOCTURNAL / RATED -20C / SERIAL 0000417.
